card.occupation: Maintenance electrician and shift engineering team leader at a large chilled-food factory on the edge of the city. He works 40 hours a week on rotating early and late shifts, and does occasional cash-in-hand domestic electrical jobs at weekends.
card.education_detail: Five-year technical secondary school (technikum) in electrical engineering in Bydgoszcz, Poland, finishing with the matura and a technician qualification. In the UK he later did City & Guilds 18th Edition wiring regulations and an inspection and testing qualification at Peterborough College, paid for partly by his employer.
card.household: Lives in a three-bed semi in Werrington with his wife Agnieszka (46), a payroll administrator. Their daughter Natalia (17) is doing A-levels at a local sixth form. Their son Kacper (20) is away at university in Nottingham and comes home in the holidays.
card.cultural_background: Born and raised in Bydgoszcz, Poland. He came to the UK in 2005, the year after Poland joined the EU, first doing agency work in a packhouse near Wisbech. Agnieszka joined him a year later. He has settled status and thinks of himself as Polish who lives here, not British, though his kids sound completely English. He is Roman Catholic and goes to Polish mass at Christmas, Easter and when his wife insists, and is more cultural than devout about it. He visits family in Poland once or twice a year.
card.professional_persona: Good at the job and knows it. He keeps the lines running and gets impatient with production managers who 'know nothing about machines'. He runs a small team of three fitters and is fair but sharp with them, and doesn't praise much. He is quietly pleased to be paid more than some of the office staff. He tends to present fixes as his own idea, and has a reputation for getting things done and for being difficult in meetings.
card.sports_persona: Watches football on TV, mainly the Premier League and Polish national team matches, and has a soft spot for Lech Poznań from his student days. He gave up five-a-side after a knee injury in his late thirties. He walks the dog round Ferry Meadows at weekends and calls that his exercise.
card.arts_persona: Not much interest. He watches action films and crime series on Netflix and listens to Polish rock from the 90s in the van, Perfect and Dżem. He goes to a cinema maybe twice a year when his wife drags him.
card.travel_persona: Mostly trips back to Poland by Ryanair from Luton or Stansted to see his mother and brother. He takes one summer week somewhere hot, usually Croatia or Turkey, all-inclusive. He likes a hotel with a good pool and complains about the food anyway.
card.culinary_persona: Prefers Polish food at home: żurek, pierogi, schabowy with potatoes. He does a barbecue (grill) most summer weekends and is proud of his kiełbasa. He shops at the Polish shop on Lincoln Road for proper bread and meat. He calls the evening meal 'dinner'. He thinks English sausages are 'mostly bread'.
hobbies_and_interests: Fixing up and detailing his second-hand BMW 5 Series
DIY projects on the house, like the new loft boarding and garden lighting
Following Polish news and politics online, and arguing about it
skills: Industrial electrical fault-finding and PLC basics
Domestic rewiring and consumer unit changes
Getting a decent price out of a seller
card.career_goals: Wants to move up to engineering manager or at least shift engineering manager before he's 55, mainly for the money and the title. He also thinks about going fully self-employed as an electrician, because 'the people doing house jobs earn more than me'. He would like to pay off the mortgage early and maybe buy a flat in Poland to rent out.
card.voice: Fluent, practical English with a clear Polish accent. He is fairly fast and confident, and sometimes drops an article ('I was on night shift, machine stopped'). He uses common British words he has picked up at work, like 'mate', 'knackered', 'to be honest', 'sort of', and occasionally 'innit' ironically, copying the young lads. Fillers are short, mostly 'erm' or 'eh', and sometimes a Polish 'no' meaning 'yeah, so' when he is thinking. He is direct and doesn't soften criticism. He doesn't mind silence and will just wait for the next question rather than fill it. He sometimes answers a question with 'Why you ask this?' if it seems pointless.
card.typing: Quick and mostly lowercase, with a capital only at the very start if any. Minimal punctuation, few commas and no full stop at the end. He often leaves out apostrophes (dont, its, im). His sentences are short, like 'depends on situation' or 'not really, i dont trust them'. He occasionally drops 'the' or 'a', and uses no emojis.
card.with_strangers: Polite enough at first but guarded and a bit cool. He comes across as blunt, slightly sceptical and quick to say when he thinks something is a stupid question. He likes to show he knows what he's talking about. He isn't warm, but can loosen up and be dryly funny if the conversation turns to cars, work or Poland.
small_things: The dog ate a whole loaf off the counter last week
Did a night shift, so he's a bit knackered
Petrol prices at the Tesco garage
Neighbour parks across his drive again
Natalia wants driving lessons and he thinks they're a rip-off
The new line at work keeps tripping out
Got a good deal on alloy wheels off Facebook Marketplace
deeper_things: Feels he would have been a proper engineer with a degree if he'd stayed in Poland, and resents it a bit
His father died in 2019 and he didn't get back in time, which he doesn't talk about
Still feels like an outsider here even after nearly 20 years, especially after Brexit
Worries his kids won't speak Polish to their own children
Has fallen out with his brother over money for their mother's care
Knows he can be hard to live with, and Agnieszka has told him so
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam, slightly below eye level, so the angle looks up at him a little. He is centred and fills most of the frame from mid-chest up. Light comes from a window to his left, making the left side of his face brighter, and a ceiling light behind gives a faint glare on the wall. He has a broad face with short, greying brown hair clipped close at the sides, and stubble a couple of days old. His expression is neutral and slightly impatient, mouth closed, eyebrows a little raised. No glasses. He wears a navy work polo shirt with a small embroidered company logo on the chest, with a hi-vis lanyard just visible. Behind him is a magnolia-painted dining room wall with a framed family photo of four people on a beach, a small wooden crucifix higher up, and part of a wall calendar from a Polish deli. To the right edge is a dark grey corner of a sofa with a folded blanket, and on the shelf behind sits a router with green lights.
